answer: Rotating Authorship Duty: each epoch the VRF beacon pulls live identities onto an exam-writing shift. The setter drafts one adversarial question anchored to an assigned knowledge shard, a haven for quality; a public panel grades clarity and difficulty, and two weak drafts in a row suspend earning. Outside shifts, an identity stays active only by solving strangers' drafts. Clone farms must field a thousand real question-writers across shards, since recycled or near-duplicate drafts cluster under corpus fingerprint and get rejected, so scale costs human judgment every round.
